name: Canada
snapshot: Canada hit back with tariffs of its own after Trump imposed 50 percent duties; in October 2026 Albertans voted three to one to stay in Canada as trade talks picked up.
culture: Canada defines itself by its bilingualism, with French-speaking Quebec a distinct nation within it, and by an official multiculturalism; more than a fifth of residents were born abroad. Hockey is the national passion. First Nations, Inuit and Métis cultures have gained recognition after a reckoning with residential schools. Toronto and Montreal are major hubs for film, music and AI research.
society: Canada exports oil, minerals, timber and cars, three-quarters of them to the United States, which makes the trade war an existential threat. Housing costs have soared, especially in Toronto and Vancouver. Public healthcare is a point of national pride, though waiting times are long. Immigration targets were cut in 2024 after a population surge.
situation: Canadians have long joked that their national identity is "not American." In 2025, when Trump called Canada the "51st state" and slapped tariffs on it, the joke became a political movement: Canadians boycotted American goods and holidays, and Mark Carney, a former central banker who had never held elected office, won an election on the promise to stand up to Washington. In 2026, the fight became a trade war.

In July, Trump announced 50 percent tariffs on about $20 billion of Canadian goods, accusing Canada of "discriminatory treatment" of US dairy, alcohol and autos. After marathon talks, Carney walked away on 22 August, saying the US had demanded at the last minute that Canada restrict its trade deals with other countries. Asked if Canada was in a trade war, he said: "You're at war when you get attacked" (Al Jazeera). Three in four Canadians backed the decision (AFP via EWN). Trump said he would double tariffs on Canadian cars to 50 percent from January. On 8 September Canada's retaliatory tariffs of up to 50 percent took effect on about C$28 billion of US goods, from steel to furniture; lobster and fresh fish were dropped after pressure from fishermen (News on AIR). Hanging over all of it is the USMCA free-trade pact, which Trump has refused to renew as is. In happier news, the Gordie Howe bridge between Windsor and Detroit finally opened in July, a reminder of how intertwined the two economies are.
power: A federal parliamentary democracy and constitutional monarchy, with the British king represented by a governor-general. The prime minister leads the party with the confidence of the 343-seat House of Commons; the ten provinces control health, education and natural resources.
holders: Prime Minister Mark Carney (Liberal), in office since March 2025.

update.html: On 19 October Albertans voted by about three to one to stay in Canada in a provincial referendum, a result Prime Minister Mark Carney hailed as a choice for unity. On 23 October Trump said he would lift some of his 50 percent tariffs on Canadian goods while adding new tariffs on dozens of other products, and on 26 October Carney said trade talks had picked up because Washington was moving toward Canada's position.
